summary: Replaces the tandem master cylinder and reservoir. The source procedure explicitly covers the K4M; brake lines must be bled after refitting.
safety: Brake fluid damages paint and nearby components; contain spills and protect surrounding surfaces.
Use approved lifting/support equipment and keep the hydraulic circuit clean.
tools: Two-post lift or approved vehicle supports

removal.text: Disconnect the battery negative terminal, remove the battery tray and required intake components, then remove the left-front wheel-arch liner for access.
Drain the reservoir with a syringe, unplug its level connector, and disconnect the clutch-feed hose and brake pipes while catching fluid.
Undo the servo mounting nuts and withdraw the master cylinder and reservoir together; separate the reservoir if it is being reused.

installation.text: Fit new master-cylinder seals and seat the reservoir correctly. Align the master cylinder with the servo pushrod before tightening.
Reconnect the hydraulic pipes and clutch-feed hose, refit access parts, then bleed the brake circuit and check carefully for leaks.

checks: Confirm the pedal is firm and the fluid level is correct after bleeding.
Check all pipe unions and the master-cylinder/servo interface for leakage.

name: Brake servo (vacuum booster)
summary: Removes and refits the brake booster. The source explicitly includes K4M and gives different pushrod reference dimensions by steering side.
safety: Brake fluid can spill during master-cylinder removal; protect paint and electrical parts.
Do not dismantle the sealed booster or pull its pushrod apart.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery negative terminal and remove the master cylinder following its separate procedure.
Disconnect the brake-pedal clevis pin from the booster pushrod in the cabin. Remove the access cowl clips and booster mounting screws, then withdraw the booster.

installation.text: Before installation, verify the pushrod reference dimension for the vehicle steering side. Refit in reverse order and tighten the booster screws to the sourced torque.
Refit the master cylinder, reconnect the battery and bleed the brake circuit.

checks: Verify the pedal/booster linkage moves freely and the brake circuit is leak-free.

name: ABS/ESP hydraulic control unit
summary: K4M-specific hydraulic-unit removal/refit procedure for ABS variants 760 or 761. Access is extensive and requires diagnostic brake bleeding.
safety: Brake fluid is corrosive to paint; cap open hydraulic connections immediately.
If air conditioning is fitted, refrigerant recovery and recharge require suitable service equipment; do not vent refrigerant.
Do not energize the ABS unit with hydraulic pipes disconnected.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery negative terminal and hold the brake pedal down with a suitable depressor to limit fluid loss.
Where fitted, recover the refrigerant with proper service equipment. Remove the right-front access parts and cowl/intake components required by the K4M procedure.
Disconnect the ABS controller connector and the hydraulic pipes, keeping the ports clean and capped. Remove the support assembly, then separate the hydraulic unit from its support.

installation.text: Mount the hydraulic unit and support, reconnect the pipes and controller, and position the controller earth lead with its wires pointing downward.
Refit disturbed intake and air-conditioning parts with sound seals, reconnect the battery, and bleed the brakes using the diagnostic tool.

checks: Run the diagnostic bleed routine and confirm the brake circuit is free of air and leaks.
Confirm the ABS/ESP controller communicates without relevant faults.

name: Rigid brake pipes and unions
summary: Identifies the brake-pipe connection standard and replacement-parts restriction. The fetched reference page does not provide a pipe-replacement torque or a complete renewal procedure.
safety: Do not improvise pipe fittings; an incorrect connection can cause brake failure.
Keep the hydraulic system clean and bleed it using the applicable service procedure after opening it.

installation.text: Install only the matching catalogued pipe and unions, then bleed the opened hydraulic circuit using the applicable service procedure.

checks: Inspect for leaks under brake pressure and confirm normal pedal feel.

name: Brake pedal and bracket
summary: Pedal removal varies by steering side. Right-hand-drive work includes removal of the brake pedal box and explicit airbag-system precautions.
safety: For right-hand-drive work involving the dashboard/column, lock the airbag control unit with the diagnostic tool before starting.
Never work on pyrotechnic restraints near heat or flame.
Do not strike the pedal crash-release feature; inspect the fuse plate and replace a deformed pedal box.

removal.text: Remove the driver-side lower trim and disconnect the brake-pedal position sensor. Separate the clevis pin from the booster pushrod and remove the pedal/bracket fasteners.
For right-hand-drive vehicles, follow the airbag-safe procedure: isolate the battery, lock the restraint controller with the diagnostic tool, and remove the column and pedal assemblies as specified.

installation.text: Refit the pedal and linkage without disturbing the crash-release mechanism; tighten the clevis bracket fasteners to the sourced torque.
Refit and adjust the pedal-position sensor, restore the restraint system as prescribed, and reconnect the battery.

checks: Confirm the pedal returns freely and the brake lamps operate.
On applicable right-hand-drive vehicles, verify the airbag controller is unlocked and has no new faults.

name: Brake-pedal position sensor
summary: The brake-pedal position sensor is a quarter-turn fitting with automatic adjustment; the fetched procedure does not explicitly identify it as the stop-lamp switch.
safety: Do not force the sensor body or its electrical connector.

specs.label: Sensor adjustment
specs.value: Self-adjusts to pedal position; pull the sensor end fully out before fitting

removal.text: Disconnect the sensor electrical connector, rotate the sensor counter-clockwise to release it, then withdraw it from the pedal bracket.

installation.text: Pull the sensor end fully out to its minimum position, fit it into the bracket and turn it clockwise to lock. Reconnect the plug.

checks: Confirm the sensor is locked in its bracket and the connector is secure.

name: Parking-brake cables
summary: Renews the mechanical parking-brake cables and sets cable adjustment by sheath-stop color; check that the rear wheels turn freely with the brake released.
safety: Support the vehicle securely before working beneath it.
Release the parking brake before disconnecting the cables from the rear calipers.
tools: Rule or caliper for cable adjustment

removal.text: Remove the centre console, disconnect the cable adjuster nut, and free both cables at the lever and rear calipers. Note their original routing before withdrawing them.

installation.text: Route the replacement cables correctly and engage their casing stops fully in the body and caliper brackets. Replace the retaining nut and set the specified dimension according to the stop color.
Cycle the parking-brake control to take up slack, then reinstall the centre console.

checks: Confirm the parking-brake lever arm clears its stop by the specified amount.
With the brake released, verify the rear wheels rotate freely.

name: Parking-brake lever and switch
summary: Removes and reinstalls the cabin parking-brake lever and switch, including the cable adjustment connection.
safety: Chock the vehicle and ensure it cannot roll before releasing or disconnecting the parking brake.
tools: Rule or caliper for cable adjustment

removal.text: Remove the centre console, disconnect the parking-brake cables from the lever, remove the mounting nuts, and unplug the switch.

installation.text: Refit the lever, reconnect its switch and cables, and tighten the mounting nuts to the sourced torque. Replace the cable adjuster nut and set cable adjustment by sheath-stop color.

checks: Check lever return and cable movement, and verify that the rear wheels turn freely with the brake released.

name: Steering rack assembly
summary: The rack is removed with the front subframe. The source gives its mounting fastener torque and requires wheel/column centering and steering sensor calibration.
safety: Secure the steering wheel in the straight-ahead position before disconnecting the intermediate shaft.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal before electrical work.

Remove the front subframe using its separate procedure, then remove the steering-rack mounting screws and withdraw the rack.

installation.text: Fit the rack with new specified subframe, rack-bracket and collapsible-yoke fasteners. Keep the wheels straight and center the steering column before reconnecting the yoke.
Refit the subframe, reconnect the battery, perform wheel alignment, and use diagnostic equipment to learn the steering torque and angle sensor.

checks: Verify steering is centered and moves smoothly from lock to lock.
Initialize the xenon headlamp system if fitted.

name: Steering column and intermediate shaft assembly
summary: The intermediate shaft, steering-wheel shaft and column form a non-dismantleable assembly. The source provides a length check, not a component overhaul procedure.
safety: Never pull on the intermediate shaft after a collision.
Center and secure the steering wheel before separating the collapsible yoke. The fetched section does not provide a steering-wheel airbag removal procedure.
tools: Diagnostic tool for steering sensor calibration

safety: Do not dismantle or repair individual parts inside the electric steering assembly.
If two operators are needed for mechanical diagnosis, disconnect the battery as directed by the source.

safety: Never support or lift the vehicle using a lower control arm.
Support the radiator and subframe before releasing their fasteners.
Lock the steering wheel before disconnecting its collapsible joint.

removal.text: Set the front wheels straight, center and lock the steering wheel, then disconnect the battery negative terminal. Support the radiator/crossmember and the subframe.
Remove the wheels and undertrays, disconnect wheel-speed sensor wiring and separate the steering tie rods, lower joints and anti-roll-bar links.
Support the subframe, release its crossmember and body attachments, and lower the assembly carefully.

installation.text: Replace the specified subframe and arm fasteners, position the radiator crossmember with the sourced spacer thickness, and refit the assembly.
Tighten only the identified fasteners to their sourced values. Restore the battery, perform wheel alignment and steering sensor learning, and initialize xenon lamps if fitted.

checks: Confirm all harnesses and sensor connectors are secured and not trapped.
Perform alignment and steering torque/angle calibration after the work.

name: Rear axle beam assembly
summary: Removes and refits the rear axle beam with springs and connected hardware. The vehicle must be secured to the lift and the axle supported during lowering.
safety: Secure the vehicle to the lift with a safety strap to prevent imbalance.
Do not lift or support the vehicle by the rear axle beam.
Tighten lower shock fasteners only with the vehicle resting on its wheels.

removal.text: Secure the vehicle on the lift, place a brake-pedal depressor, remove the rear wheels and unclip the parking-brake cables. Disconnect the brake hoses and wheel-speed sensor connectors.
Support and strap the axle, release the lower shock mounts and springs as instructed, then lower the supported beam from its body pivots.

installation.text: Reinstall the beam and its components, route brake lines and parking-brake cables correctly, and reconnect the wheel-speed sensors.
Set the shock-mount center distance to the sourced installation dimension while positioning the axle. Tighten pivot mounts and brake-hose screws, then refit springs and shocks.
Lower the vehicle onto its wheels before tightening the lower shock mounts; reinstall the protective shield and wheels.

checks: Bleed the brake circuit if it was opened and inspect for leaks.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery negative terminal and remove the lower trim, cabin fuse/control unit and left air duct as required for access.
Twist and disconnect the clutch start- and end-of-travel switches, detach the master-cylinder ball joint, remove the pedal-platform nuts and withdraw the pedal assembly.

installation.text: Refit the pedal platform and tighten its retaining nuts to the sourced torque. Pull both switch plungers to their minimum position, fit them and rotate them clockwise to lock.
Reconnect all plugs and hydraulic connections; bleed the clutch circuit if it was opened, then reconnect the battery.

checks: Confirm both pedal-position switches register and the clutch pedal returns smoothly.
